title: Modules courbes elliptiques en caractéristiques ≠2 : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck is studying 'octahedral configurations' Δ in a P^1-bundle X/S. These are étale divisors of degree 6, and the model case is Δ = {0, ∞, ±1, ±i} ⊂ P^1_S over a base where 2 is invertible and i exists. Earlier in these notes the six points come up via elliptic-curve moduli: they are the cusps of X(4) ≅ P^1, permuted by PSL_2(Z/4) ≅ S_4. The previous page showed that the stabilizers of the three 'diagonals' {0,∞}, {1,-1}, {i,-i} are cyclic of order 4, isomorphic to μ_4.

On this page he shows that the pointwise stabilizer of a non-diagonal pair is trivial, taking {∞, -1}.
- An automorphism fixing ∞ is affine, z ↦ az + b. Fixing -1 forces b = a - 1, so the map is z ↦ az + (a-1).
- Such a map must permute {0, 1, i, -i}. Suppose it is not the identity, so a ≠ 1.
- z = 0: a - 1 ∈ {1, i, -i}, so a ∈ {2, 1+i, 1-i}.
- z = 1: 2a - 1 ∈ {0, i, -i}, so a ∈ {1/2, (1+i)/2, (1-i)/2}.
- These two sets are already disjoint, so the identity is the only possibility. The checks at z = i (a ∈ {(1-i)/2, 1-i, -i}) and z = -i (a ∈ {(1+i)/2, 1+i, i}) are redundant confirmations.
- By homogeneity (Γ is transitive on such edges), the same holds for every 2-element subset of Δ other than Δ_1, Δ_2, Δ_3.

Consequences:
- The decomposition Δ = Δ_1 ⊔ Δ_2 ⊔ Δ_3 is intrinsically characterised by the 'isotropy' relation of the previous page, so it is Γ-invariant. Hence Γ = Aut(X, Δ) embeds in Aut_oct(Δ), and in fact in Aut^+_oct(Δ), the direct (rotation) symmetries.
- Equality holds because the rotation group of the octahedron (≅ S_4) is generated by its three cyclic subgroups of order 4 (the axis rotations), and these lie in Γ.

This prepares the next page's definition of a 'regular' octahedral structure: an étale degree-6 divisor with fixed-point-free involution σ_Δ such that Aut^+_oct(Δ) acts compatibly on X.
errors: The aborted argument 'it must induce a permutation of order ≤2 … so a^4=1' is confused; Grothendieck abandons it and the marginal scribbles about a^4 = ±4, 1/4 are dead ends. The final case analysis is correct.
Tacitly a ≠ 1 is assumed when excluding a - 1 = 0 and 2a - 1 = 1; this is fine since one seeks a nontrivial element.
The checks at z = i and z = -i are superfluous: the z = 0 and z = 1 conditions already have empty intersection.

ideas.what: Pointwise stabilizer of a non-diagonal pair in the octahedral configuration {0,∞,±1,±i} ⊂ P^1 is trivial; the octahedral (diagonal) decomposition is intrinsic, and Aut(P^1, Δ) ≅ Aut^+_oct(Δ) ≅ S_4
ideas.modern_name: Octahedral group O ≅ S_4 ≅ PSL_2(Z/4) acting on the cusps of X(4); the classical Klein octahedral configuration

ideas.what: Rotation group of the octahedron generated by its three cyclic order-4 axis subgroups
Relative (over a base S) notion of octahedral configuration as an étale degree-6 divisor in a P^1-bundle, with Γ = Aut^+_oct(Δ) as a finite étale group scheme twisted form of S_4
ideas.modern_name: Twisted forms of the octahedral configuration / S_4-torsors attached to level-4 structures on the moduli of elliptic curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Implicit in the moduli of elliptic curves with level structure (Deligne–Rapoport, Katz–Mazur); explicit relative treatment uncertain

deep.surprise_reason: A routine verification of the classical fact that the automorphism group of the octahedral six-point configuration on P^1 is the rotation group S_4. Correct and careful, but nothing new; the relative framing over S is set up on neighbouring pages, not here.
transcription_corrections: In the z = i line the second value should read 1-i (= 2/(1+i)), not '(1-i)/1 [?]'. The full set is a ∈ {(1-i)/2, 1-i, -i}; the interlinear note '1:(1-i/2)' records that 1/(1+i) = (1-i)/2.
In 'si l'automorphisme qui induit par l'identité' the sense is 'si l'automorphisme n'est pas l'identité' (if the automorphism is not the identity).
'la division [?] Δ' is likely 'le diviseur Δ'.
